subject: Recap: CloudMed decision criteria & procurement path
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Jun 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: CloudMed decision criteria & procurement path

Jordan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned while you take this to procurement/legal.

Key decision criteria (as discussed)
- Latency SLO: you mentioned target of p95 latency for inference under typical burst ~200ms; please confirm whether this is 512-token or 1k-token baseline.
- Cost guardrail: target unit economics of ~$0.0012 per token-equivalent (your target to finance) — confirm if this is a hard ceiling or guidance.
- Deployment: CloudMed preference today is Dedicated (VPC) for PHI handling, but open to Redwood Hosted if procurement/controls are faster.
- SLA: expectation is 99.9%+ uptime and audit logging for the inference path; we attached an SLA draft.

Who we believe needs to be engaged
- Economic buyer: Procurement lead (Priya Shah) — can you confirm?
- Security/compliance: Andrew Li (engineering security) + InfoSec questionnaire (we included a one-page security matrix).
- Legal: standard review for Data Processing Addendum and contract terms.

Requested confirmations / asks
1) Please confirm the economic buyer and expected approval window (weeks).
2) Confirm the latency baseline (512 vs 1k tokens) and whether p95 200ms is acceptable or needs to be lower.
3) Confirm whether CloudMed will require on-prem/air-gapped or VPC-only Dedicated deployment.
4) If procurement requests an NDA or PoC statement, we can share the POC brief and a proposed 2-week test plan.

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft.pdf (SLA + fallbacks), security-matrix-cloudmed.xlsx (summary for your security team), poc-proposal-brief.pdf (high-level POC and success criteria)

Proposed next steps
- Jordan to introduce Priya & Andrew on this thread (if not already included) — they can scope procurement/security asks.
- Redwood to send a short POC plan and a sample SLA for procurement to review (attached).
- Target follow-up: 1 week to confirm stakeholders and 3 weeks for procurement timeline if only standard review needed.

Appreciate a quick reply with the confirmations above so we can prioritize the right resources.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com]

Subject: Re: Recap: CloudMed decision criteria & procurement path

Rachel — thanks for the clear summary. I’ve looped in Priya (procurement) and Andrew (security) on the next message but can answer a few items now:

- Economic buyer: confirmed — Priya Shah (procurement). She owns vendor approvals and contract sign-off.
- Latency baseline: the 200ms p95 we mentioned is for a 512-token inference; if that moves to 1k tokens we’d expect ~1.5-2x degradation. So please size POC around 512 tokens.
- Cost: $0.0012/token is our target ceiling for initial budgeting (finance prefers lower but will tolerate up to that).
- Deployment: we prefer Dedicated with VPC peering for PHI controls; we will only evaluate Hosted if Dedicated approvals slip longer than 6 weeks.
- Security requirements: SOC 2 Type II is required; Andrew will follow up with the vendor questionnaire and a list of required evidence.
- Procurement timeline: rough expectation is 4–8 weeks if no major legal redlines; vendor onboarding (security review) is usually the gating item.

We agree a 2-week technical POC is best. Priya — can you confirm procurement lead timing and whether you need an NDA before a POC?

Thanks,
Jordan
Director of Product
CloudMed Health

Thanks Jordan/Rachel — looping in Andrew as well as requested. A few quick procurement notes from my side:

- Timeline: target 6 weeks for vendor approval is realistic if the security questionnaire and SOC 2 report are provided promptly.
- NDA: we generally require a mutual NDA before provisioning PII/PHI test data; we can sign a standard one (DocuSign preferred).
- Contracting: procurement will need a draft order form with the expected monthly commit and an outline of the POC scope so finance can estimate spend.
- Acceptance criteria: procurement and finance will want a cost estimate for production (monthly committed GPUs) and the expected unit economics at the committed level.

Please send a proposed POC scope + an indicative commit-level pricing plan and we’ll slot it into the procurement calendar.

Subject: Re: Recap: CloudMed decision criteria & procurement path — PoC sizing and rough pricing

Priya / Jordan — quick note on POC sizing and indicative commit ranges to help procurement/finance: 

- PoC: 2-week dedicated environment with a small Reserved pool (2x A100-equivalent GPUs) supporting sustained load at 512-token p95 target. We’ll keep logging and KV-cache enabled to mirror production.
- PoC cost (Redwood estimate): ~$6k–9k for the 2-week Dedicated environment (includes reserved GPUs + network egress + support). We can tighten after we agree on throughput profile.
- Example committed options (monthly):
  - Entry: 4 GPUs reserved — ~ $18k/month (good for teams with low concurrency, cost per 1k tokens ~ $0.0009)
  - Standard: 8 GPUs reserved — ~ $32k/month (better throughput; ~ $0.0006 per 1k tokens with batching)
  - Enterprise: 16+ GPUs — custom pricing, we’ll provide after workload sample.

Notes: these are ballpark numbers to put procurement on the same page. If CloudMed wants tighter unit economics we can propose quantized model variants and cache/batching patterns that typically shave 20–40% off per-token costs.

Next steps I’ll take from here:
- Draft a two-page POC scope + runbook and share via Drive (link included).
- Send a redlined sample order form + SLA for procurement to review (attached).
- Coordinate a short architecture call with Andrew to validate network/VPC peering requirements.
